stories.headline: Looking back at local news from the archives
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at stories from the Fenland archives. In September 1986, pool players in Nordelph raised £415 for charity. The funds were collected during a 24-hour marathon at the Chequers pub, held in memory of former player Christopher Clingo.

Also in the archives, we recall an incident from 2016 involving a performer at Mr Fips Wonder Circus in King’s Lynn. The UK’s last human cannonball, 26-year-old Shane Beare, was taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital after breaking both ankles during a stunt at Knights Hill. Mr Beare later stated that he lost concentration during the performance, which was witnessed by an audience of around 300 people.

stories.headline: Peterborough United drawn against Bradford in Carabao Cup
stories.brief: Peterborough United are set to travel to Bradford for their upcoming Carabao Cup fixture. The club, known as Posh, will face the Bantams in the next round of the competition. Further details regarding the date and kick-off time for the match are expected to be confirmed by the clubs in due course. Fans are advised to keep an eye on official announcements for ticket information and travel arrangements as the team prepares for the away trip.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire businesses advised to check fire safety
stories.brief: Business owners across Cambridgeshire are being encouraged to carry out a review of their current fire safety measures. The advice comes following a report from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News. Local firms are being urged to ensure their premises remain compliant with safety standards to protect staff and property.

stories.headline: Developer appeals butterfly park planning refusal
stories.brief: A developer is challenging a decision to refuse planning permission for a proposed butterfly park. The project, which has prompted concerns from local residents, was previously rejected by planning authorities. The developer is now seeking to overturn that outcome. Further details regarding the appeal process have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Council leader criticises waste management contract
stories.brief: The leader of the council has described the local authority's annual waste management deal as a mess. The contract, which is valued at 36 million pounds per year, has come under fire from the council’s leadership. No further details regarding the specific nature of the issues or potential changes to the service have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech Statute Fair returns to town centre
stories.brief:
The historic Wisbech Statute Fair is back in the town centre for its annual visit. Mayor Lucie Foice-Beard officially opened the event yesterday evening at the Church Terrace car park, accompanied by fellow councillors. The fair, which has a tradition spanning over 750 years, is presented by the Eastern Section of the Showmen's Guild and features a variety of rides, games, and food stalls.

Residents can visit the fair tonight and tomorrow from 5pm until late. Weekend opening hours are from 2pm until late on both Saturday and Sunday. The event will conclude this Sunday.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man jailed for theft and criminal damage
stories.brief:
A 38-year-old man from King’s Lynn has been sentenced to six weeks in prison following a series of offences. Scott Manning, who is of no fixed address, was arrested in Downham on Tuesday. He appeared at Norwich Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday, where he admitted to stealing over £500 worth of make-up and other items from a chemist. 

In addition to the theft, Manning pleaded guilty to criminal damage after spitting on the seat of a police vehicle during his arrest. Alongside his custodial sentence, the court has ordered him to pay a fine of £124.

stories.headline: Three Lincolnshire shops closed over illegal tobacco sales
stories.brief: Three shops in Lincolnshire have been forced to close following the sale of illegal cigarettes. The closures were confirmed in reports by the BBC. No further details regarding the specific locations of the businesses or the duration of the closures have been released at this time.

stories.headline: One-year prison sentence for Gucci thief
stories.brief: A thief has been sentenced to one year in prison following a conviction for stealing Gucci goods. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the outcome of the case. No further details regarding the location or timing of the theft have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: New mobile mechanic service launches across West Norfolk
stories.brief:
A husband and wife team have launched a new mobile vehicle repair business serving residents in King’s Lynn, Downham Market, Swaffham, and Wisbech. Neil and Jemma Fleckney, who have 40 years of combined trade experience, are offering a fully insured service that carries out repairs, diagnostics, and servicing at a customer’s home or workplace. 

The couple stated that their new venture, West Norfolk Mobile Mechanics, aims to reduce the inconvenience of traditional garage visits for those living in rural areas. The service also includes pre-MOT inspections and a collection and delivery option for MOT testing. The founders say they hope to provide a more affordable and convenient alternative for local drivers.

stories.headline: Peterborough City Council reports budget overspend
stories.brief: Peterborough City Council has confirmed it is currently overspending its budget. The local authority says the financial pressure is being driven by the rising costs of providing children's care services.

stories.headline: Bus service under threat in Cambridgeshire village
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire village faces the potential loss of its bus connection, despite the recent installation of new shelters. The facilities, which cost sixteen thousand pounds, were intended to support local transport infrastructure. However, the future of the bus route serving the area remains uncertain. Residents are now waiting to see if the service will continue to operate.

stories.headline: Long-serving vicar announces retirement
stories.brief: A local vicar is preparing to step down from their role following a lengthy period of service. While the individual is set to retire from their current position, they have already confirmed plans for a new mission. Further details regarding the nature of this upcoming project have been described as having a "wow" factor. No specific date for the departure has been announced at this time.

stories.headline: Council faces £800,000 loss on bank site project
stories.brief: Local authorities are expected to lose £800,000 on a regeneration project involving a former bank site. According to reports, the financial shortfall stems from the development scheme. No further details regarding the specific location or the timeline for the project have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn performing arts group reaches national final
stories.brief:
Theatretrain King’s Lynn has been named a finalist in the 2026 What’s On 4 Kids Awards. The local performing arts company is competing in the Most Loved Music, Dance or Performing Arts Activity category. The winners are decided by family votes, with tens of thousands cast across the UK this year.

Kate Whyborn, who has led the group since 2019, expressed pride in the nomination and thanked the families who supported them. The results will be announced at a ceremony in Leicester on November 26, hosted by Jonathan Bremner. Theatretrain holds weekly sessions for young performers at Springwood High School. Further information is available on the Theatretrain King’s Lynn website.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on missing 27-year-old man
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are asking for the public's help to locate a missing 27-year-old man. Officers have issued an appeal for information regarding his whereabouts. Anyone who may have seen him or who has details that could assist the investigation is urged to contact the police.

stories.headline: Questions raised over Cambridgeshire pothole contract transparency
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire County Council is facing questions regarding the transparency of its contracts for pothole repairs. The local authority has been asked to provide further clarity on how these agreements are managed. The inquiry follows reports concerning the oversight of road maintenance work across the region. No further details regarding the specific nature of the contracts or the council's response have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: New classic vehicle auction launches in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Anglia Car Auctions in King’s Lynn has introduced a new sale format to meet rising interest in modern classic cars. The business, based on Beveridge Way, is launching the ACA Marketplace Classics auctions to provide a dedicated platform for vehicles that fall between their traditional classic and modern sales. 

The new event will take place five times a year, with the inaugural sale scheduled for Saturday, September 26. Entries for the auction are now open. The company, which has operated since 1995, continues to offer in-person viewing and live drive-throughs for bidders. Further details on how to enter a vehicle can be found on the Anglia Car Auctions website.

stories.headline: Peterborough school issues reassurance following stabbing incident
stories.brief: A school in Peterborough has contacted parents to provide reassurance following a stabbing incident involving a pupil. The school has addressed concerns regarding the event, though no further details about the circumstances or the condition of those involved have been released at this time. Officials are working to support the school community as the situation is managed.

stories.headline: Haddenham Steam Rally declared a success despite wet weather
stories.brief: Organisers have described the recent Haddenham Steam Rally as a great show. The event took place despite challenging conditions caused by poor weather. Further details regarding the rally's attendance or specific activities have not been released.

stories.headline: Concerns raised regarding land condition in South Holland
stories.brief: Residents in South Holland have expressed concerns regarding the current state of a piece of local land. Reports indicate that members of the public have raised issues about the condition of the site, though specific details regarding the location or the nature of the problems have not been provided. Local authorities have yet to issue a formal response to these complaints. We will bring you further updates on this story as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Water supply issues reported in Chatteris
stories.brief:
Residents in Chatteris are experiencing ongoing problems with their water supply. Reports indicate that the service has been intermittent, leading to frustration among those living in the town. Local households have faced repeated disruptions to their water access, though the cause of the supply issues remains unclear. 

Those affected are advised to monitor official updates from their water provider for further information regarding the situation and expected restoration times.

stories.headline: Wonder Circus arrives in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
The Wonder Circus ‘It’s Show Time’ 2026 tour has arrived in King’s Lynn. The big top is now open at Knights Hill, next to the Rising Lodge Farm Shop, with performances running until Sunday, September 27. The show features acrobats, performers, and traditional circus acts. 

Following the King’s Lynn residency, the circus will move to the Denver playing fields from Wednesday, September 30, through to Sunday, October 4. The on-site box office is open daily from 10am until 8pm for cash purchases. For further information, you can call 07719 877422. The Lynn News is also running a competition for VIP tickets; details on how to enter can be found on their website.

stories.headline: Police appeal following Cambridge collision
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has issued an appeal for information following a road traffic collision in Cambridge. Officers are currently seeking witnesses or anyone with relevant details regarding the incident. Those who can assist with the ongoing enquiries are encouraged to contact the police directly.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Under-21s draw with Bristol City
stories.brief: The Peterborough United Under-21 side finished level in their recent fixture against Bristol City Under-21s. The match concluded with a scoreline of three goals apiece. Highlights from the encounter have been released by Bristol City Football Club.

stories.headline: Immigration checks conducted at East Cambridgeshire takeaways
stories.brief: Immigration enforcement officers have carried out checks at takeaway businesses across East Cambridgeshire. The operation resulted in the discovery of individuals working illegally within the district. Further details regarding the specific locations visited or the number of people involved have not been disclosed by authorities at this stage.

stories.headline: Police appeal for footage following Long Sutton brawl
stories.brief: Police are asking for the public’s help following a fight in Long Sutton that left three people injured. Officers are seeking video footage of the incident to assist with their ongoing enquiries. Anyone who may have recorded the altercation or who has information regarding the event is encouraged to come forward to help with the investigation.

stories.headline: Several individuals sentenced at court in March
stories.brief: A number of offenders have been handed prison sentences following recent court proceedings in March. Among those receiving custodial terms were an electrician convicted of indecent exposure and a man found guilty of rape. The cases were reported by The Hunts Post.

stories.headline: Wisbech street drinking ban extended for three years
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council has extended a public spaces protection order in Wisbech for another three years. The measure, which aims to reduce anti-social behaviour, makes it an offence to consume alcohol in specific areas, including Tillery Fields, King’s Walk, St Peter’s Church gardens, and the memorial garden on The Crescent.

Under the order, enforcement officers can request that individuals hand over alcoholic drinks in town centre locations outside of private or licensed premises. Failure to comply is an offence. Cabinet members approved the extension this week, noting that while incidents have decreased since the order was first introduced in 2017, the powers remain necessary to help manage ongoing issues. The current order will now remain in place until 2029.

stories.headline: Police release CCTV following King’s Lynn ram raid
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police have released CCTV footage following a ram raid at the Costa Coffee shop on St Nicholas Retail Park in North Lynn. The incident occurred at 2:50am on August 27, when a vehicle was driven into the front of the building, causing significant damage. A charity box was stolen during the burglary.

The vehicle involved, a stolen silver Vauxhall Mokka, was later recovered on Camfrey. Officers are now appealing for help to identify a person seen in the footage. Anyone who recognises the individual’s clothing or gait is asked to contact Norfolk Police quoting reference 36/64220/26. Information can also be provided anonymously through Crimestoppers. A man in his 40s has been arrested and released on bail.

stories.headline: Eye scans could predict heart condition
stories.brief: Researchers at University College London have identified a potential new method for detecting atrial fibrillation. A study suggests that routine eye scans may be able to identify signs of the heart condition up to four years before a formal clinical diagnosis is made. The findings indicate that these scans could offer an early warning system for patients. Further information regarding the study is available through University College London.

stories.headline: New murals appear at Ely underpass
stories.brief: The underpass in Ely has been decorated with its first set of murals. The artwork marks the launch of the city’s new ‘Free Wall’ initiative. The project aims to provide a designated space for street art within the local area.

stories.headline: Police appeal following supermarket theft
stories.brief: Officers are asking for the public's help to identify three men in connection with a theft at a supermarket. Police are currently investigating the incident and have released an appeal for information to assist with their enquiries. Anyone who may be able to identify the individuals involved or who has relevant information is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Whittlesey residents' group responds to claims
stories.brief: A residents' group based at Saxon Pit in Whittlesey has expressed shock following a recent claim described as 'vocal'. The report, which originated from the BBC, highlights the group's reaction to the statement. No further details regarding the nature of the claim or the specific circumstances surrounding the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Immigration checks conducted at East Cambridgeshire takeaways
stories.brief: Immigration enforcement officers have carried out checks at a number of takeaway businesses across East Cambridgeshire. The operation resulted in the discovery of individuals working illegally within the district. Further details regarding the specific locations visited or the number of people involved have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: Union warns of potential food shortages following Princes factory strike
stories.brief: The Unite union has warned that industrial action at the Princes factory could result in food shortages. The dispute involves staff at the site, with the union suggesting that the walkout may impact the supply chain. No further details regarding the specific timeline of the strike or the products affected have been released at this stage. Residents across the Fens are advised to monitor the situation for any potential impact on local availability.

stories.headline: Police receive map detailing location of buried woman
stories.brief: A man has provided police with a map indicating the location where he buried a woman. The details were reported by the BBC. No further information regarding the identity of the individuals involved or the specific location of the burial site has been released at this time.

stories.headline: Peterborough United progress in Carabao Cup
stories.brief: Peterborough United have advanced to the next round of the Carabao Cup following a dramatic victory over Barnsley. The match ended in a three-all draw after regular time. The tie was ultimately decided by a penalty shootout, which Peterborough won seven-six.

stories.headline: Opposition grows to East Cambridgeshire station closure plans
stories.brief: Residents in East Cambridgeshire have expressed strong opposition to proposals that could see a local station close. Reports from the Ely Standard indicate that members of the public have described the potential closure as madness. No further details regarding the specific location of the station or the timeline for the proposed changes have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Long Sutton headteacher defends school incentive scheme
stories.brief: The headteacher of a school in Long Sutton has spoken out in support of a new incentive programme. The initiative, which has been described as a "duvet day," is being defended by school leadership following recent attention. No further details regarding the specific nature of the scheme or the school involved have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over proposed energy plant in Chatteris
stories.brief: Residents in Chatteris have expressed concerns regarding a proposed energy plant for the town. Reports indicate that local people are worried about the potential for unpleasant odours resulting from the development. The plans for the new facility have been highlighted by the March Chatteris Whittlesey News. No further details regarding the project's timeline or specific operational plans have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire firm and director fined for illegal trading
stories.brief: A Lincolnshire-based company and one of its directors have been ordered to pay tens of thousands of pounds following a case of illegal trading. The penalties were issued after legal action regarding the firm's business practices. Further details on the nature of the trading offences have not been disclosed, but the court ruling confirms significant financial sanctions have been imposed on both the business and the individual involved.

stories.headline: Damage revealed following Iceland roof collapse in March
stories.brief: New images have been released showing the scale of the damage caused by a roof collapse at the Iceland store in March. The photographs provide a clearer look at the aftermath of the incident at the retail premises. There is currently no further information regarding the cause of the collapse or any potential reopening date for the site. Residents are advised to monitor local updates for any changes to access in the area.

stories.headline: Peterborough United progress in cup competition
stories.brief: Peterborough United have secured their place in the fourth round of the competition following a dramatic encounter against Barnsley. The match ended in a three-all draw after regular time, forcing the tie to be decided by a penalty shootout. Peterborough United ultimately triumphed seven-six on penalties to progress to the next stage.

stories.headline: Immigration checks carried out at Ely and Soham takeaways
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has reported that illegal workers were discovered during recent checks at takeaway businesses in Ely and Soham. Officers conducted the visits as part of an enforcement operation in the area. No further details regarding the specific businesses involved or the number of individuals detained have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Lorry breakdown causes A17 closure
stories.brief: Motorists travelling on the A17 have faced disruption following a vehicle breakdown. Reports indicate that the road was closed after a lorry became stuck, causing delays for those using the route. Traffic flow in the area has been affected by the incident. Drivers are advised to check for any remaining congestion before setting off on their journeys through the Fens.

stories.headline: Road repair trial to begin on peat surfaces
stories.brief: A trial project aimed at repairing roads built on peat is set to get underway. The initiative will test new methods for maintaining these specific types of road surfaces, which are common across the region. Further details regarding the exact locations and the duration of the work have not yet been confirmed. Residents and motorists are advised to look out for updates as the trial progresses.

stories.headline: Wisbech street-drinking ban extended by council
stories.brief: Fenland District Council has approved an extension to the public space protection order covering Wisbech town centre. The measure, which allows authorities to seize alcohol in areas like Tillery Park and St Peter and Paul Church, was set to expire next week. While 98 per cent of survey respondents supported the renewal, many residents expressed concern that the rules are not being enforced. Councillor Steve Tierney noted that public drinking remains a daily issue, despite police reports indicating a 41 per cent drop in alcohol-related crime since the order was first introduced in 2017. Residents have reported feeling intimidated by the ongoing anti-social behaviour in the town centre.

stories.headline: Residents invited to shape future of West Norfolk healthcare
stories.brief:
People living in West Norfolk are being asked to share their views on the future of local health services. Healthwatch Norfolk has launched a public survey to help inform a new clinical strategy for hospitals across the region, including the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn.

The consultation seeks feedback on current experiences, the delivery of care, and priorities for future generations. Responses will be shared with healthcare professionals and community representatives to help guide long-term planning. This initiative comes as plans for a new hospital in King’s Lynn continue to develop. Residents can participate in the survey online to ensure their experiences help influence how local NHS services are delivered over the next two decades.

stories.headline: Planning application submitted for new Cambridgeshire landmark hub
stories.brief: A formal planning application has been submitted to develop a new landmark hub in a Cambridgeshire town. The proposal, referred to as Buttondown, is currently being put forward by the local council. No further details regarding the specific location or the nature of the facility have been released at this stage. Residents are advised to monitor official council planning portals for updates as the application progresses through the review process.

stories.headline: New traffic calming measures planned for March
stories.brief: Drivers in March should prepare for upcoming changes to local roads. New traffic calming measures are set to be introduced in the town, with the primary aim of improving road safety for the community. Further details regarding the specific locations and the timeline for these installations have not yet been released. Residents are advised to keep an eye out for future updates as the project progresses.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire councillor defends crematorium funding
stories.brief: An East Cambridgeshire councillor has defended the 13-million-pound cost of a new crematorium. The official described the funding used for the project as being left over money. No further details regarding the development have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Approval granted for 70 new homes in Long Sutton
stories.brief: A development of 70 new homes in Long Sutton has been given the go-ahead. Planning permission was granted following an agreement between the developer and local authorities to make changes to the original proposal. The project is set to proceed after these adjustments were finalised.

stories.headline: Illegal tobacco and vapes seized in Fenland
stories.brief: Police have confiscated a large quantity of illegal cigarettes and vapes from a shop in the Fenland area. Officers carried out the operation to remove the illicit items from circulation. No further details regarding the specific location or any potential arrests have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Local residents share concerns over hospital services and transport
stories.brief:
Readers of the Lynn News have raised concerns regarding the future of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Discussions are currently underway regarding the potential relocation of maternity and intensive care services, prompting local debate about the hospital's long-term role in the region.

In other news, a new bus route has been introduced to improve transport links for several Norfolk villages. The service connects Crimplesham, Fincham, Marham, and Narborough with Swaffham. Operating every two hours from Monday to Saturday, the route includes a stop at Tesco and costs three pounds each way, with bus passes accepted.

stories.headline: Police appeal following Peterborough collision
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has issued an appeal for information following a road traffic collision in Peterborough. Officers are currently looking for witnesses or anyone with relevant details regarding the incident. Those who can assist with the ongoing enquiries are being asked to contact the force directly.

stories.headline: Sutton Bridge man completes wing walk for Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
A Sutton Bridge man has raised £1,200 for the endoscopy unit at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Brian Moss completed a sponsored wing walk at Wickenby Airfield last month to thank staff for the care his wife received at the hospital late last year. 

Mr. Moss was supported in his fundraising by family, friends, and his colleagues at Bridge Hardware, who contributed through sponsorship and a World Cup sweepstake. Lead nurse manager Helen Smith thanked Mr. Moss for his efforts, noting that the funds will help enhance patient care. Those interested in supporting the hospital charity can find more information on the Queen Elizabeth Hospital website.

stories.headline: Peterborough Nepalese community launches flood appeal
stories.brief: The Nepalese community in Peterborough is spearheading a new fundraising appeal to support those affected by recent flooding. Organisers are calling on local residents to contribute to the relief efforts. Further details regarding how to donate or assist with the campaign are expected to be released as the initiative gets underway.

stories.headline: Retrospective planning application submitted for East Cambs showman's yard
stories.brief: A planning application has been submitted seeking retrospective approval for a showman's yard located in an East Cambridgeshire village. The proposal, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, asks for official permission for the site’s current use. No further details regarding the specific location or the timeline for a decision have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Air ambulance attends incident in Long Sutton
stories.brief: An air ambulance has landed in Long Sutton. The arrival of the emergency aircraft was reported by the Spalding South Holland News. No further details regarding the nature of the incident or the condition of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Penny Farthing marks 115 years in town
stories.brief: A local landmark is celebrating a significant milestone this week. The Penny Farthing has officially reached its 115th year in the town. The historic site continues to be a notable feature for the local community.

stories.headline: Coffee morning to be held at Wisbech church
stories.brief: Residents are invited to a community coffee morning at St Peter and St Paul’s Church in Wisbech this weekend. The event takes place in the church hall on Saturday, October 10, running from 10am until 12 noon. Visitors can enjoy tea, coffee and a selection of homemade cakes. There will also be a variety of stalls available for attendees to browse throughout the morning.

stories.headline: Historic cobblestones restored at King’s Lynn museum
stories.brief:
The first phase of a restoration project at True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum in King’s Lynn is now complete. Volunteers from the Lynn and West Norfolk Archaeological Society spent two weeks uncovering and restoring original cobblestones in the museum’s courtyard. The historic flooring was discovered after the removal of the Activity vessel, which has since been relocated to Dersingham.

The work has revealed the thresholds of previously demolished cottages, offering a glimpse into the lives of local fishing families from a century ago. Museum officials say the project was made possible through grants and private donations. Future plans for the site include building replica cottages for educational use, an initiative estimated to cost £500,000.

stories.headline: Police cordon in place at Peterborough playing fields
stories.brief: Officers have established a cordon at a playing field in Peterborough following an incident. The Peterborough Telegraph reports that the area has been taped off while police attend the scene. No further details regarding the nature of the incident or any potential injuries have been released at this time. Residents are advised that access to the site is currently restricted while investigations continue.

stories.headline: Conservative Party secures majority in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: The Conservative Party has gained a majority on East Cambridgeshire District Council. This shift in the local political landscape follows the defection of a former Liberal Democrat councillor to the Conservative group. The change in party affiliation has altered the balance of power within the local authority.

stories.headline: Public meeting scheduled regarding Spalding flat development
stories.brief: A public meeting is set to take place to discuss plans for new flats in Spalding. The proposal has been described in reports as a "stealth" plan for the town. Residents are invited to attend the session to learn more about the development and share their views on the project. Further details regarding the specific time and venue for the meeting have not yet been released.

stories.headline: South Cambridgeshire District Council planning meeting scheduled
stories.brief: The South Cambridgeshire District Council planning committee is set to meet in March 2026. Residents are advised that this upcoming session will address local planning matters within the district. Further details regarding the specific agenda or the exact date of the meeting have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Tom Aspinall vacates UFC heavyweight title
stories.brief: UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall has vacated his title. The decision follows reports of ongoing issues with his vision. No further details regarding his condition or future career plans have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Ely nursery receives positive first Ofsted report
stories.brief: A nursery in Ely has been awarded a strong rating across all categories following its first inspection by Ofsted. The education watchdog assessed the facility and found it met high standards in every area reviewed. This marks a successful debut for the nursery, which has now officially completed its initial regulatory evaluation.

stories.headline: Long Sutton pensioner remanded in custody
stories.brief: A 74-year-old resident from Long Sutton has been remanded in custody. The decision was made following a court appearance at Lincoln Magistrates’ Court. No further details regarding the case have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Road surface issues reported in the Fens
stories.brief: Motorists in the Fens are facing difficulties following recent resurfacing work on a local road. Reports indicate the condition of the surface is poor enough to trigger car alarms on passing vehicles. The situation has been described as horrendous by those travelling through the area. Local residents and commuters are advised to take care when using the route.

stories.headline: Man from Ipswich dies in Cambridgeshire van crash
stories.brief: A man from Ipswich has died following a van crash in Cambridgeshire. The incident was reported by the East Anglian Daily Times. No further details regarding the location or the circumstances of the collision have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police investigate meat theft in Spalding
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are investigating the theft of meat from a shop in Spalding. Officers are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the incident at the town centre store. No further details regarding the suspects or the value of the goods taken have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Prison officer jailed following relationship with inmate
stories.brief: A prison officer has been sentenced to time in jail after engaging in a relationship with an inmate. The case was brought forward by Cambridgeshire Constabulary. No further details regarding the location of the prison or the length of the sentence have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Traffic disruption following lorry incident in Spalding
stories.brief: Drivers in Spalding are being advised of potential delays following an incident at a busy roundabout. A lorry has lost its load, causing an obstruction in the area. Motorists are encouraged to approach the junction with caution and allow extra time for their journeys while the scene is cleared. No further details regarding the cause of the incident or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Corn Exchange to light up for domestic abuse charity
stories.brief:
The King’s Lynn-based Pandora Project is marking its 13th anniversary with a special illumination of the town’s Corn Exchange. The building will be lit in purple this Saturday, September 19, ahead of Domestic Abuse Awareness Month in October. 

The charity provides specialist support to women and children across North and West Norfolk affected by domestic abuse. Figures from Norfolk County Council show nearly 11,400 domestic abuse-related crimes were recorded in the county during 2023/24. Organisers hope the display will raise awareness and remind those in need that local support services remain available. Further information can be found on the Pandora Project website.

stories.headline: Conservative majority secured in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: The Conservative Party has gained a majority on East Cambridgeshire District Council. This shift in control follows the defection of a former Liberal Democrat councillor. The change in political balance was confirmed in reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News.

stories.headline: Police investigate armed robbery at Long Sutton newsagent
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are investigating an armed robbery at a newsagent in Long Sutton. A person armed with a knife entered the shop and stole a quantity of cash and cigarettes. Officers are currently looking into the incident. Anyone with information regarding the robbery is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Field fire reported in Whittlesey
stories.brief: Emergency services have responded to a large fire in a field located in Whittlesey. Details regarding the cause of the blaze or any potential impact on the surrounding area have not yet been released. Residents are advised to remain aware of their surroundings if travelling near the site of the incident. We will provide further updates as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Knife sculpture to visit Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire is set to host a knife monument. According to the Cambridgeshire Constabulary, the sculpture is described as a powerful installation. Further details regarding the specific locations or dates for the monument's arrival in the county have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Police respond to three-vehicle collision in Fenland
stories.brief: Emergency services have been called to the scene of a road traffic collision in a Fenland town. The incident involved three vehicles. No further details regarding the exact location or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police appeal for help finding missing woman with links to Wisbech
stories.brief:
Lincolnshire Police are asking for the public’s help to locate a missing 27-year-old woman. Rhiannon, who also uses the name Hope, was last seen in the Spalding area on Thursday, September 10. She is known to have connections to both Wisbech and Peterborough.

At the time of her disappearance, she was wearing a blue jumper, black leggings, and possibly black flip-flops. Officers have expressed concern for her welfare and are urging anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to come forward. You can contact the police by calling 101, quoting incident number 131 of September 12, or by emailing force.control@lincs.police.uk.

stories.headline: Ely records highest safety improvements from 20mph speed limits
stories.brief: New data indicates that the introduction of a 20mph speed limit in Ely has resulted in the most significant road safety improvements across Cambridgeshire. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the lower speed restrictions have proven more effective in the city than in other parts of the county. Local residents and commuters are advised that these measures continue to impact traffic flow and safety standards throughout the area.

stories.headline: Man hospitalised following three-car collision
stories.brief: A man has been taken to hospital with serious injuries following a road traffic collision involving three vehicles. Emergency services were called to the scene to assist those involved. No further details regarding the location or the condition of other individuals have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Driver jailed following serious collision
stories.brief: A motorist has been sentenced to prison after causing serious injuries in a high-speed road accident. Cambridgeshire Police confirmed the outcome of the case, which involved two victims. No further details regarding the location or the specific date of the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Five Cambridgeshire businesses named for underpaying staff
stories.brief:
The government has identified five companies based in Cambridgeshire for failing to pay their employees the legal minimum wage. The businesses were named following an official review into pay practices across the region. 

The Department for Business and Trade has highlighted these cases as part of a wider effort to ensure workers receive their correct legal entitlement. Further details regarding the specific firms involved and the total amount of back pay owed to staff can be found via the Ely East Cambridgeshire News website.

stories.headline: Police release CCTV images following attempted Whittlesey burglary
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police have released CCTV images as part of an ongoing investigation into an attempted burglary in Whittlesey. Officers are appealing for information from the public to help identify those involved in the incident. Anyone who recognises the individuals pictured or has relevant information is encouraged to contact the police. Further details regarding the investigation can be found on the Cambsnews website.

stories.headline: North Lynn man bailed following assault on parents
stories.brief:
A 40-year-old North Lynn man has appeared in court after assaulting his elderly parents. Peter Goff, of Loke Road, was collected by his parents from Swaffham on the morning of April 21st following a night of drinking. Upon returning to their home in Great Dunham, Goff became abusive, slapping his father and physically assaulting his mother.

Lynn Magistrates’ Court heard that the couple are struggling to cope with his behaviour. The case has been adjourned until November 12th for a pre-sentence report. Goff has been released on conditional bail, which prohibits him from contacting his parents or visiting their home.

stories.headline: Ten high-rise buildings in region remain fitted with unsafe cladding
stories.brief: New figures reveal that ten high-rise buildings across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough are still fitted with unsafe cladding. The data, reported by the Ely Standard, highlights ongoing safety concerns for residents living in these properties. While the report identifies the number of affected buildings, it does not specify their exact locations. Local authorities and building owners are expected to address these fire safety risks as part of national remediation efforts. Residents are advised to check with their building management for further information regarding the safety status of their specific property.

stories.headline: Positive coronavirus tests confirmed at Lincolnshire school
stories.brief: A school in Lincolnshire has reported several positive cases of coronavirus. The news was confirmed by the institution following reports from local media. No further details regarding the specific location of the school or the number of individuals affected have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Field fire reported in Whittlesey
stories.brief: Emergency services have responded to a large fire in a field in Whittlesey. Details regarding the cause of the blaze or any potential impact on the surrounding area have not yet been released. Residents are advised to remain aware of their surroundings if travelling near the site. We will bring you further updates as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Long Sutton Library to reopen this May
stories.brief: Lincolnshire County Council has announced that Long Sutton Library is scheduled to reopen its doors to the public this May. Further details regarding the specific date of the reopening or the library's operating hours have not yet been provided by the local authority. Residents are advised to look out for additional updates from the council as the reopening date approaches.

stories.headline: Campaign launched to save Whittlesey Scaldgate Centre
stories.brief: A campaign is underway to protect the Scaldgate Centre in Whittlesey. Local residents are currently fighting to save the facility from closure. Further details regarding the future of the site have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Students across East Cambridgeshire receive GCSE results
stories.brief: Students throughout East Cambridgeshire are heading to their schools today to collect their GCSE results. The Ely Standard is providing live coverage as teenagers across the district find out their grades. Families and pupils are currently receiving the outcome of their exams following months of study.

stories.headline: Local vicar contributes to report on Covid-19 impact
stories.brief: A local vicar has played a significant role in a new report examining the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on the region. The findings, which highlight how the area was affected by the health crisis, were recently featured by the Spalding South Holland News. The report aims to provide insight into the challenges faced by local communities during the pandemic period.

stories.headline: Man jailed for controlling behaviour in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced to prison for controlling his partner. The case was brought to court following an investigation by Cambridgeshire Constabulary. No further details regarding the length of the sentence or the location of the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Emergency services attend incident in Spalding town centre
stories.brief: Emergency crews were called to Spalding town centre following reports of a man on a roof. Lincolnshire Police and other emergency services attended the scene to respond to the situation. No further details regarding the individual or the outcome of the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire Fire Service reports 20 incidents in a single day
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service says crews have been pushed to their limits following a busy period. Firefighters were called out to 20 separate incidents within the space of 24 hours. The service has highlighted the pressure placed on resources during this high volume of callouts.

stories.headline: Arts programme to return to Cambridgeshire libraries
stories.brief: An arts programme is set to make a comeback across Cambridgeshire this autumn. The initiative will be hosted at 23 libraries throughout the county. Residents are encouraged to check their local branch for further details on the upcoming schedule of events.

stories.headline: Roadworks scheduled for A17 between Holbeach and Sutton Bridge
stories.brief: Drivers in the Fens are being advised that resurfacing work is set to begin on the A17 this weekend. Lincolnshire County Council has confirmed that the maintenance project will take place on the stretch of road located between Holbeach and Sutton Bridge. Motorists travelling through the area should prepare for potential disruption while these improvements are carried out.
